# Wave 24 acceptance (65f5649) — ACCEPT

## 1. Ruling the open findings
All seven wave-24 findings are **fixed** in 65f5649:

- **F02-9 fixed.** `Get-EndpointHealth` gives a quota-without-reset an `Until = Hit + 60 min` (common.ps1:4721-4745); provider rows now call `Get-PreflightVerdict -RosterWalk` (codex-providers.ps1:305, 349), and the hook consumes the `-Short -Json` line built from the same walk — one verdict everywhere (QUOTA60 tests, incl. +61 min and clear-on-success).
- **F02-10 fixed.** `-Short -Json` emits one `entries[]` record per roster entry (position/provider/model/kind/reason/short; common.ps1:5427-5462, codex-providers.ps1:409-424); multi-model labels no longer collapse in the hook line.
- **F02-11 fixed.** `Get-RosterAvailability` builds `Get-EndpointGroups` over ALL roster entries and propagates an auth/quota outage across the group (common.ps1:5438-5452); `Get-PanelPlan` still groups runners only for scheduling (5273-5293), as D16 decides.
- **F03-4 fixed.** The verdict regex is gone; the hook reads `obj.line` from the providers JSON and only falls back to the first output line (hook.ps1:58-71).
- **F03-5 fixed.** It became the intended display/run unification, not a second rule: rows, `-Short`, hook and the walk all consume `Get-PreflightVerdict -RosterWalk`.
- **F04-9 fixed.** `Select-PanelMembers` now has `-NoNetwork` and judges every entry (common.ps1:5159-5200); the hook runs `codex-providers -Short -Json -NoNetwork` — no network sign-in.
- **F04-10 fixed.** Nothing is cut (D17: complete phrases, local time + relative hint); the count has the third state ("…, N out, M not checked", common.ps1:5465-5508).

All other listed ids are **not-checked**: they concern the companions wave (R14–R16 panel draw, ratings, roles, `-Require`), which is not implemented at 65f5649.

## 2. New defects in wave 24 (what I verified vs inferred)
Verified in code: the continuation gates (`-ContinueSec` 0, unknown thread, survivors, tree change, quota/auth in the killed turn's own stream — codex-consult.ps1:2999-3022), muse's `-Fresh` guard before every turn incl. the continuation (666, 2621; muse adapter 3757-3769), the codex `resume <thread>` argv mirroring the main turn (3031-3038 vs 2372-2392), thread verification of the continuation (3070, 3088), salvage conditions and the partial file/footer/resume command (3402-3456), `-Thread` accepting a killed agy/muse candidate via `partial_reply` (Find-ThreadEntry), the second tree check after all extra turns (3345-3352), purpose timeouts and `-Range` (788-802, 900-918, 1046-1064, 2290-2292), the panel member inheritance and guard growth (837-843, 1238-1267, common.ps1:5326-5332), and the availability surfaces above. harness-visibility has exactly 76 checks incl. CONTAGY/CONTMUSE and the F15-1 mid-run auth change; run-all.ps1 registers it.

Three minor notes, none blocking (findings #1–#3): the continuation prompt omits the output contract that the denial retry re-sends (matters only for prompt-only schema endpoints, where the thread still holds it); `Read-CodexSalvage` can list an id-less tool call twice (started+completed fall back to different `#k` keys); the hook/listing repeats per-entry identity+health work up to three times and one `codex login status` (15 s timeout) per codex provider, so the documented "about one second" can be exceeded on large rosters/ledgers.

## 3. Verdict
**ACCEPT.** No blocker or major remains; all wave-24 prior findings are fixed and the new code is internally consistent with the documented D14–D17 behavior. Blockers: none.

Unproven and first-run observations are listed below; believe exit 0 only after the checklist is seen on a real run.

## Requested checks
- RC1 — `pwsh -NoProfile -File tests/run-all.ps1` (repo root; workspace-write; ~10–15 min): expect every harness green incl. visibility 76; settles the claimed suite under both shells when repeated with powershell.exe.
- RC2 — `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-providers.ps1 -Short` in a real repository (read-only; measure time): expect the one line and a latency well under the hook budget; settles finding #3.
- RC3 — a real `codex-consult.ps1 -Purpose chore -TimeoutSec 20 -ContinueSec 60` against a slow live prompt-only endpoint (workspace-write): expect kill → continuation → structured reply; settles findings #1 and the real-rollout question.

findings.claim: The timeout-continuation prompt re-sends only the brief, a finish-now sentence and the consultation id; unlike the denial retry it does not re-send the output contract/schema lines, so on prompt-only schema transports (MiMo, undeclared hosts) the continuation must rely on the killed thread's memory of the format, raising the chance of a prose (no-verdict) reply after a timeout.
findings.trigger: A prompt-only endpoint's main turn is killed at its timeout and the continuation answers without re-stating the JSON contract.

evidence.observation: contParts adds promptParts[0], the finish-now text and the consult id only

findings.verification: Run a real consultation against a prompt-only endpoint with a timeout that kills the main turn and inspect whether the continuation reply parses as structured.
findings.remedy: Add the schema/output-contract block to the continuation prompt for prompt-only transports (as the denial retry does), or state the reliance on thread context as a decision.

findings.claim: Read-CodexSalvage increments $k for both item.started and item.completed and uses "#$k" as the id fallback, so a tool item without an id is inserted into the partial file's tool list twice (once per event) instead of once.
findings.trigger: A killed codex turn whose event stream contains a tool item.started/item.completed pair with an empty id.

evidence.observation: $k++ per started-or-completed line; the completed branch adds again because '#<n>' differs from the started key

findings.verification: Feed a synthetic stream with one id-less command_execution started+completed pair and count the tool lines in the formatted partial body.
findings.remedy: Derive the fallback key from the item's stable fields (type+index within that type) or only insert on item.completed/first-seen.

findings.claim: The availability view resolves every roster entry's identity and health up to three times (single walk, Get-RosterAvailability, provider/engine rows) and runs one codex login status (15 s timeout) per codex provider, so the hook's documented 'about one second' cost can be exceeded on large rosters or ledgers, though it stays read-only and network-free.
findings.trigger: SessionStart in a repository with many roster entries, several codex providers and large session ledgers.

evidence.observation: walk, Get-RosterAvailability and the row loops each call Resolve-ReviewerIdentity/Get-EndpointHealth per entry/provider
the hook spawns the full listing; only the ~1 s figure is documented

findings.verification: Time codex-providers.ps1 -Short -NoNetwork in a repository with an 11-entry roster and multi-megabyte ledgers.
findings.remedy: Cache identity/health per provider label within one listing invocation, or document a wider latency bound for the hook.

first_run_checklist: First acceptance run's ledger entry shows timeout_sec 3600, timeout_source "purpose", continue_sec 900 (and the console 'Timeout: 3600 s (the default of purpose acceptance); continuation after a timeout kill: up to 900 s').

On the first real timeout kill, the console shows 'the main turn was killed at <t> s of <T> s; one continuation turn on thread <id> (up to <C> s)' and the ledger gains timeout_continue {thread, wall_seconds, outcome, events, usage}.

If the continuation answers, bridge_outcome is exactly 'usable reply (after a timeout continuation)' and the scoreboard counts it as USABLE; if it also dies, handoffs/NN-<engine>-<slug>.partial.md exists with per-turn headings and a 'killed at …; thread <id> - continue with …' footer whose printed resume command actually resumes that thread.

SessionStart hook prints one 'codex-consult: …' line identical to codex-providers.ps1 -Short in the same repository, and 'endpoint health:' names that repository's ledger directory with the task/consult counts.

After a real 429 without Retry-After: the provider row, -Short line, hook and roster walk all say out with 'usage limit hit <iso>, reset unknown; retry after <iso>', and the endpoint is selectable again 61 minutes after the hit.
